mainTopic: When several מוספים fall on one day (the trumpets, the songs, and the refutation of רבי אחא), and which day's קרבנות to mention on חול המועד in חוץ לארץ
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge. Besides the change in the song, the fats of the ראש חודש offering were placed in a special spot to show that ראש חודש was set on time, so why have both signs? The גמרא answers that the Temple used two signs so that more people would notice. Next, a ברייתא teaches that when שבת and ראש חודש fall together, the trumpets are blown only once for all the מוספים. This is a full refutation (תיובתא) of רבי אחא. אביי and רב אשי each explain how the verse ״וּבְרָאשֵׁי חׇדְשֵׁיכֶם״ teaches this. A second ברייתא lists the לוים's song for each day of חול המועד and says that when שבת falls on one of those days, the last song, ״ימוטו״, is dropped. This also refutes רבי אחא. רב ספרא and רב פפא give memory aids for the order of the songs. The גמרא then asks what רבי אחא's own sources meant: רבינא says they teach longer blasts, and the רבנן of קיסרי say they teach more trumpeters. Finally, the גמרא asks how communities in חוץ לארץ, who keep two days of יום טוב, mention each day's קרבנות on חול המועד. אביי drops the second day's portion, רבא drops the seventh with a ברייתא supporting him, and אמימר says both doubtful days each day.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן explains the special placement of the fats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge by quoting רבי יוחנן. He said the fats of the ראש חודש offering were placed in a special spot so people would know ראש חודש was set on time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: the fats were placed there so people would know that ראש חודש was set at its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing a challenge it began on the previous amud. It quotes רבי יוחנן's reason for a visible sign in the Temple showing that it was ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the placement of the fats already told people that ראש חודש was set on time, then a second sign seems unnecessary. That second sign is the change in the Levites' song. The question is why the Temple would need both.
steps.confusionAlert: This line does not start a new topic. It is the last piece of a challenge that began on the previous amud, so read it as part of the question, not as a new teaching.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
to let people know that the New Moon was set at its proper time.
phrases.notes: This explains why the fats of the ראש חודש offering were placed in a special spot.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֵידַע שֶׁהוּקְבַּע רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ בִּזְמַנּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the song is changed in order to publicize ראש חודש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sign already existed in how the fats were placed, so a second sign through the song seems unnecessary.

steps.title: There were two signs
steps.stepSummary: The Temple used two separate signs, so anyone who saw either one would know.
steps.simpleTranslation: We make two signs. Whoever saw this one saw it, and whoever saw that one saw it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Both signs were used on purpose so that more people would notice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not everyone was in the right place to see where the fats were put, and not everyone heard the song. Having two signs means more people would find out that ראש חודש was set on time. So the extra sign is useful, not wasted.

phrases.english: We make two signs.
Whoever sees this one sees it,
phrases.notes: For example, someone who hears the song.

phrases.english: and whoever sees that one sees it.
phrases.notes: For example, someone who sees where the fats were placed.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Both signs are needed because each reaches different people.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One sign is enough, so the second is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two signs were used on purpose so that more people would see one of them.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the trumpets are blown once for all the מוספים
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר שמואל teaches that when שבת and ראש חודש fall together, the trumpets are not blown separately for each מוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: They object: רבא בר שמואל taught, 'I might think that just as the trumpets are blown for שבת on its own and for ראש חודש on its own, so too they would be blown for each separate מוסף when the days fall together. Therefore the verse says ״וּבְרָאשֵׁי חׇדְשֵׁיכֶם״.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that challenges רבי אחא. It says that on a day with several מוספים, the trumpets are blown only once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a normal שבת or a normal ראש חודש, the trumpets are blown for that day's מוסף. One might think that when both fall together, they blow twice, once for each מוסף. The verse teaches that they do not. This clashes with רבי אחא's view, from the previous amud, that each מוסף gets its own separate treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: the additional offering of a special day

phrases.english: They objected, for Rava bar Shmuel taught:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל כְּשֵׁם שֶׁתּוֹקְעִין עַל שַׁבָּת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: I might think: just as they blow for Shabbat on its own
and for the New Moon on its own,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ יִהְיוּ תּוֹקְעִין עַל כׇּל מוּסָף וּמוּסָף —
phrases.english: so too they would blow for each and every additional offering (when the days fall together).
Therefore the verse says: 'and on your New Moons' (Numbers 10:10).
phrases.notes: This teaches that they blow only once for all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against רבי אחא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אחא's view that each מוסף gets its own separate treatment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says there is only one blowing of the trumpets for all the מוספים together, not a separate one for each.

steps.title: רבי אחא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא fully refutes רבי אחא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רבי אחא! It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the result of the challenge: רבי אחא's view cannot stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תיובתא means a full defeat with no answer offered. The גמרא first says it as a claim and then repeats it to confirm it. רבי אחא's position is rejected.
steps.whatToRemember: When שבת and ראש חודש fall together, the trumpets are blown once for all the מוספים, and רבי אחא is refuted.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Rabbi Acha!
It is indeed a refutation.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אחא's view is rejected. There is one trumpet blowing for all the מוספים.

steps.title: How does the verse teach this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the words ״וּבְרָאשֵׁי חׇדְשֵׁיכֶם״ show that the trumpets are blown only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask how the ברייתא learned its rule from the verse. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse simply says 'and on your New Moons.' It is not obvious how that teaches one blowing for several מוספים, so the גמרא wants the exact reasoning.

phrases.english: What is the derivation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the verse cited in step 3 teaches its rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the verse teaches that the trumpets are blown once.

steps.title: אביי: all months are compared to each other
steps.stepSummary: The plural word compares every ראש חודש to every other. A normal ראש חודש gets one blowing, so one that falls on שבת also gets one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The verse says ״וּבְרָאשֵׁי חׇדְשֵׁיכֶם״, so all the months are compared to one another.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first explanation of the derivation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the verse speaks of all the New Moons together, they are treated the same. A regular ראש חודש has one blowing, so a ראש חודש that falls on שבת also has only one.

phrases.english: Abaye said: The verse says:
'and on your New Moons' (plural)

phrases.aramaic: הוּקְּשׁוּ כׇּל חֳדָשִׁים כּוּלָּם זֶה לָזֶה.
phrases.english: so all the months are compared to one another.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הקש between all the months: every ראש חודש gets the same single blowing.

steps.title: רב אשי: ראש השנה, the month with two heads
steps.stepSummary: The verse uses a plural word for 'heads' but a singular word for 'month.' That points to ראש השנה, which is both a new year and a new month, and still gets one blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is written 'your month' (singular) and also 'and on the heads of' (plural). Which month has two heads? You must say it is ראש השנה. And the Torah still says 'your month' in the singular, which means it is one blowing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second, different explanation of how the verse teaches one blowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראש השנה is both the start of the year and the start of the month, so it has two 'heads.' The Torah still uses the singular 'your month,' which teaches that even with two reasons to blow, there is only one blowing. The same applies to any day with several מוספים.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי and רב אשי reach the same rule (one blowing) from the same verse by different readings: אביי compares all months, while רב אשי reads the singular and plural forms.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: It is written 'your month' (singular, without a yod),
and it is written 'and on the heads of' (plural).

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵיזֶה חֹדֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי רָאשִׁים,
phrases.english: And which month has two heads?
You must say: this is Rosh Hashana,
phrases.notes: It is the start of the year and the start of the month.

phrases.english: and yet the Torah says 'your month' (singular),
so it is one (one blowing).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question that אביי answered.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The singular 'your month' used for ראש השנה, which has two 'heads,' shows there is only one blowing.

steps.title: A second proof: the songs of חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins another ברייתא against רבי אחא, which lists the Levites' song for each day of חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, it was taught: On חול המועד, on the first day what would they say? ״הָבוּ לַה׳ בְּנֵי אֵלִים״. On the second day what would they say? ״וְלָרָשָׁע אָמַר אֱלֹהִים״. On the third day what would they say? ״מִי יָקוּם לִי עִם מְרֵעִים״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a second challenge to רבי אחא. It lays out the list of songs for חול המועד, and the point of the challenge comes at the end of this ברייתא in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives one fixed song for each day of סוכות's חול המועד. As it continues, it will show how the songs were arranged when שבת fell on one of these days, which goes against רבי אחא's view. For now we are only collecting the list.

keyTerms.meaning: the intermediate days of the festival

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not complete yet. Do not look for the contradiction in these lines alone. It comes at the end of the ברייתא, in step 9.

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught in a baraita:
On the intermediate days of the Festival,
on the first day, what would they say?
'Ascribe to the Lord, you sons of might' (Psalms 29).
On the second day, what would they say?
'But to the wicked God says' (Psalms 50).
On the third day, what would they say?
'Who will rise up for me against the evildoers?' (Psalms 94).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source against רבי אחא after the first refutation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אחא's view on giving each מוסף its own separate treatment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fixed order of songs for חול המועד (completed in step 9) will show that a separate song was not added for each occasion.

steps.title: The last songs of חול המועד and what happens on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the songs for days four, five and six of חול המועד. It then says that if שבת falls on one of these days, the song ״ימוטו״ is dropped.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the fourth day, what did they say? ״Understand, you foolish ones among the people.″ On the fifth day, what did they say? ″I removed his shoulder from the burden.″ On the sixth day, what did they say? ″All the foundations of the earth are shaken.″ And if שבת falls on one of these days, ״ימוטו″ is pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it started in the previous step. The last line is the punchline that attacks רבי אחא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a חול המועד day that is also שבת, the לוים sing only the שבת song, not the holiday song too. Because one day's slot is used up, the list of holiday songs runs one day short, so the last one, ״ימוטו״, never gets sung. This shows that the extra occasion (שבת) did not add its own song on top of the holiday song. That goes against רבי אחא's view that each extra occasion gets its own addition.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle days of the festival
The song the לוים sang over the קרבנות
'Are shaken.' The opening word of the last holiday song

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think ״ימוטו″ is dropped only when שבת lands on the sixth day. The songs keep going in order on the weekdays. Whichever day is שבת gets the שבת song, so the list falls one day short and the last song, ״ימוטו″, is the one left out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the part of the ברייתא that actually disproves רבי אחא, which leads straight to the תיובתא in step 11.

phrases.english: On the fourth day, what would they say?
"Understand, you foolish ones among the people"
phrases.notes: תהלים צ״ד:ח

phrases.english: On the fifth day, what would they say?
"I removed his shoulder from the burden"
phrases.notes: תהלים פ״א:ז

phrases.english: On the sixth day, what would they say?
"All the foundations of the earth are shaken"
phrases.notes: תהלים פ״ב:ה

phrases.english: And if Shabbat falls on one of them,
"Yimotu" is pushed off.
phrases.notes: The שבת song takes that day's place, so the last holiday song drops out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם חָל שַׁבָּת בְּאֶחָד מֵהֶם, ״יִמּוֹטוּ״ יִדָּחֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that step 8 started quoting against רבי אחא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אחא בר חנינא's view that each extra occasion gets its own addition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When שבת and a חול המועד day fall together, only the שבת song is sung, not both. So the extra occasion does not get its own extra addition.

steps.title: Memory aids for the order of the songs
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא and רב פפא each give a letter-code for the order of the חול המועד songs. They disagree about whether ״בינו″ or ״הסירותי″ comes first. A further hint tells us which code belongs to which אמורא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא gave them a memory aid: ה-ו-מ-ב-ה-י. רב פפא gave them a memory aid: ה-ו-מ-ה-ב-י. And your hint is: ״אמבוהא דספרי״, 'a crowd of scribes.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a side note. The אמוראים give short letter-codes to help us remember the order of the six songs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter is the first letter of one song: הבו, ולרשע, מי יקום, בינו, הסירותי, ימוטו. רב ספרא puts ב (״בינו″) before ה (״הסירותי″), while רב פפא reverses those two. The word ״אמבוהא″ has מ, then ב, then ה, which matches רב ספרא's order. The word ״ספרי″ points to רב ספרא's name.

keyTerms.meaning: Placed on them, i.e., assigned to them
A crowd of scribes, the hint for whose code is whose

steps.confusionAlert: The first three letters (ה-ו-מ) stand for the songs of days one to three, which were listed in step 8.

phrases.english: Rav Safra placed a mnemonic on them:
"H-V-M-B-H-Y"
phrases.notes: Order: הבו, ולרשע, מי יקום, בינו, הסירותי, ימוטו

phrases.english: Rav Pappa placed a mnemonic on them:
"H-V-M-H-B-Y"
phrases.notes: Here ״הסירותי″ comes before ״בינו″

phrases.english: And your sign: "a crowd of scribes."
phrases.notes: מ-ב-ה in אמבוהא matches the order of רב ספרא

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side note on the order of the songs listed in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order of the six songs, with two versions that disagree about days four and five.

steps.title: רבי אחא בר חנינא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that this ברייתא is a full refutation of רבי אחא בר חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רבי אחא בר חנינא! It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states that the ברייתא about the songs fully disproves רבי אחא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא showed that on a combined day only one song was sung, not one for each occasion. רבי אחא's claim that each extra occasion gets its own addition cannot stand. The גמרא accepts this as final.

keyTerms.meaning: A full refutation; the view is rejected
The אמורא whose view is being rejected

phrases.english: A refutation of Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina!
It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in steps 8 and 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Extra occasions on the same day do not each get their own separate addition. רבי אחא is rejected.

steps.title: But רבי אחא brought a פסוק and a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אחא can be rejected so easily, since he backed his view with a פסוק and a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אחא בר חנינא quote a פסוק and a ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now has a loose end. If רבי אחא is wrong, what do his sources mean?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אחא did not invent his view; he based it on a פסוק and a ברייתא. Even after rejecting his ruling, the גמרא must explain those sources some other way. Otherwise they would seem to support the rejected view.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים
'But surely...' A word that opens a challenge

phrases.english: But surely Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina
was saying a verse and a baraita?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא קְרָא וּמַתְנִיתָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the refutation by pointing to רבי אחא's sources.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion in step 11 that רבי אחא is fully refuted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אחא had a פסוק and a ברייתא. These must mean something, and at first glance they seem to back his view.

steps.title: רבינא: the blasts are made longer
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that רבי אחא's sources teach that the trumpet blasts are made longer for the extra occasion. They do not teach that extra blasts are added.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The sources come to teach that we make the blasts longer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a new reading of רבי אחא's פסוק and ברייתא, so they no longer support his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sources do show that the extra occasion gets some honor. But that honor is longer blasts, not a separate set of blasts. So the sources fit the ברייתא that refuted רבי אחא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To say,' i.e., the source comes to teach

phrases.english: Ravina said:
To say that they lengthen the blasts.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אחא's sources teach that each extra occasion gets its own blasts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sources only teach that the blasts are made longer, with no extra blasts.

steps.title: The רבנן of קיסרי: more people blow
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן of קיסרי, quoting רבי אחא himself, explain that the sources teach that more trumpeters are added. The number of blasts stays the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן of קיסרי said in the name of רבי אחא: The sources come to teach that one adds more people blowing.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second, different reading of the same sources. Here the honor for the extra occasion is more trumpeters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The honor is added through more people blowing, not more blasts or longer blasts. Because this is quoted in רבי אחא's own name, it seems he himself explained his sources this way. So the sources and the ברייתא do not clash.
steps.whatToRemember: When several מוספים fall on the same day (for example שבת with ראש חודש, or שבת during חול המועד), each occasion does not get its own separate song or blasts. רבי אחא's sources only teach a way to add honor: longer blasts (רבינא) or more trumpeters (רבנן of קיסרי).

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּנַן דְּקֵיסָרִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַחָא אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: The Rabbis of Caesarea said in the name of Rabbi Aḥa:
To say that one increases the trumpeters.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן דְּקֵיסָרִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַחָא אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge in step 12, different from רבינא's.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sources teach adding separate blasts for each occasion.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sources teach adding more trumpeters, not more blasts.

steps.title: What do people outside Israel do with their doubtful days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how communities in חוץ לארץ, who keep two days of יום טוב, decide which day's קרבנות to mention on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we, who have two days of יום טוב, what do we do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new practical question, and it is setting up the answers that come next. Outside Israel we are not sure of the exact day, so which day's portion do we say?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each day of סוכות has its own קרבנות in פרשת פינחס. Those are mentioned in מוסף and read from the Torah. In חוץ לארץ the first day of חול המועד might really be day 2 or day 3 of סוכות, so we cannot be sure which portion belongs to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Two days, meaning the two-day יום טוב kept outside Israel because of doubt
How do we act? A request for practical guidance
And we, meaning those of us living in בבל or חוץ לארץ

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the songs from the earlier steps. It is about which day's קרבנות are mentioned in מוסף and read in the Torah on each day of חול המועד.

phrases.english: And we, who have two days (of Yom Tov),
phrases.notes: Refers to the communities in בבל, who keep a second day out of doubt.

phrases.english: how do we act?
phrases.notes: Which day's offerings do we mention each day?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנַן, דְּאִית לַן תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי, הֵיכִי עָבְדִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the order of the חול המועד songs to a related practical question about the daily מוסף portions in חוץ לארץ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which day's קרבנות portion is mentioned on each doubtful day of חול המועד outside Israel.

steps.title: אביי: the second day's portion is dropped
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that we follow the count of ארץ ישראל, so the second day's portion is never said.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the second day is pushed aside.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first answer. On the first day of חול המועד we say the third day's portion, because that is the correct count in Israel. The second day's portion is skipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ארץ ישראל, the first day of חול המועד is day 3 of סוכות. אביי follows that real count and mentions day 3 on that day, day 4 on the next, and so on. The result is that the portion for day 2 is never said in חוץ לארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading אמורא of בבל who often argues with רבא
The second (day's portion) will be pushed aside, meaning it is skipped

phrases.english: Abaye said: the second (day) is pushed aside.
phrases.notes: Follow the ארץ ישראל count, so the second day's portion is never mentioned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Follow the Israel count. The second day's portion drops out.

steps.title: רבא: the seventh day's portion is dropped
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that each day is said one day behind, so the seventh day's portion is the one that drops out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the seventh day is pushed aside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with אביי. On the first day of חול המועד we say the second day's portion, and every day stays one step behind. By the end, the seventh day's portion has no day left to be said on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because we stay one day behind, the seventh day's portion would fall on the eighth day. But the eighth day is שמיני עצרת, which has its own portion. So under רבא, all the portions are said in order and only the last one, the seventh, is lost.

keyTerms.meaning: A great אמורא of בבל and אביי's frequent partner in debate
The seventh (day's portion) will be pushed aside
The eighth day, a separate holiday with its own offerings

steps.whatToRemember: אביי drops an early portion (day 2) so that the later days match the true count. רבא keeps the portions in order and drops the last one (day 7).

phrases.english: Rava said: the seventh (day) is pushed aside.
phrases.notes: Run one day behind; the seventh-day portion has no place left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Say each portion one day behind. The seventh day's portion drops out.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא: when a day is pushed, the last song is dropped
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that when שבת falls during חול המועד, the seventh day's song ״ימוטו״ is the one dropped. This matches רבא's approach of dropping the last item.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that supports רבא: if שבת falls on one of the days, the song ״ימוטו״ is pushed aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support for רבא. It comes from the list of the לויים' songs for חול המועד that we saw in the earlier steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When שבת takes over one day with its own song, the remaining songs are not skipped in the middle. They keep their order, and the last song, ״ימוטו″ of the seventh day, is the one that drops out. This is the same pattern as רבא's rule: keep the order and lose the seventh.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in agreement with him, a support formula
"They will be moved," the key word of the seventh day's song (תהלים פב:ה)

phrases.english: It was taught (in a Baraita) in accordance with Rava:
phrases.notes: Introduces a supporting Tannaitic source.

phrases.aramaic: אִם חָל שַׁבָּת לִהְיוֹת בְּאֶחָד מֵהֶן,
phrases.english: if Shabbat falls on one of them (the intermediate days),
phrases.notes: שבת has its own song, which replaces the day's song.

phrases.english: "Yimotu" is pushed aside.
phrases.notes: The last (seventh-day) song drops out, not a middle one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a ברייתא for רבא's view in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that the seventh item is the one dropped
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the order of the חול המועד songs, where ״ימוטו״ is dropped when שבת falls during the festival

steps.title: אמימר's practice in נהרדעא: say both doubtful days
steps.stepSummary: אמימר set up a practice in נהרדעא of saying both possible days' portions each day, overlapping from one day to the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר made a rule in נהרדעא that they "skip and jump," saying both doubtful days each day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third approach, a practice that אמימר set up in his city. Instead of dropping any portion, each day covers both possible days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first day of חול המועד they say the portions of day 2 and day 3. The next day they repeat day 3 and add day 4, and so on. This way the correct portion is always included, no matter which way the ספק goes, and nothing is lost.

keyTerms.meaning: He instituted, meaning he set up a fixed practice
They "jump around," meaning they go back and forth and repeat the overlapping days

steps.whatToRemember: There are three approaches. אביי drops day 2. רבא drops day 7, and the ברייתא supports him. אמימר says both doubtful days every day, so nothing is lost.
steps.whyThisMatters: This question about a doubtful day comes up whenever practice in חוץ לארץ has to deal with the second-day ספק. אמימר's approach of covering both options is the basis for the common custom of mentioning both possible days.

phrases.english: Ameimar instituted in Neharde'a
phrases.notes: A local enactment.

phrases.english: that they skip back and forth (repeating the overlapping days).
phrases.notes: Each day they say both the previous doubtful day and the next one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third practical solution to the question of step 15, different from both אביי and רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In חוץ לארץ, each day of חול המועד mentions both possible days' portions, so that no portion is dropped.
